topic: Sharp tree-diagonal capacity set for the full distribution of an oracle dynamic-treatment outcome. In a finite full-history SMART with known positive randomization and Y in {0,...,K-1}, target every pmf/CDF of M=max_d Y(d) compatible with the observed law under Shahn's FFRCISTG model. Prove the local maximum-coupling characterization q attainable iff F_q is below every action-marginal CDF and q(k)<=sum_a p_a(k); recurse it over the explicit treatment tree and prove both projection and an observed-law-preserving FFRCISTG lift including dormant branches and single-world independences. After intervention-reach rescaling, derive an O(K times tree-size) polyhedral formulation linear in observed multinomial probabilities, exact membership/support dual certificates, attaining samplers, strict cross-threshold nonrectangularity, and finite-sample whole-set confidence inversion by LP for the SMART-BD oracle-remission consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: monotone residual transport proves the local iff; reach-probability rescaling linearizes observed cells; local and two-stage reduced formulations matched 880 full response-type LP support checks to 8.9e-16, including a positive two-stage obstruction. Static copula and maximum-transport results are occupied, but no recursive causal-set collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove every recursively feasible array embeds into the complete FFRCISTG counterfactual system while preserving dormant-branch consistency and single-world independences. EARLY KILL TEST: explicitly project the full two-stage binary-action, binary-response, three-outcome FFRCISTG model and compare it with the reduced formulation on heterogeneous positive kernels; any reduced feasible point without a valid lift should pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_oracle_dtr_tree_diagonal_set.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every recursively locally feasible array of oracle-maximum laws on a finite treatment tree has a single observed-law-preserving FFRCISTG extension containing all dormant counterfactual branches.

source_refs.claim: The sharpness proof selects compatible distributions branchwise and asserts that incompatible branch objects may be associated arbitrarily, without explicitly constructing the complete dormant-branch system.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: SWIGs encode the single-world counterfactual independences of FFRCISTG and extend to dynamic treatment regimes.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson and James M. Robins
source_refs.venue: University of Washington CSSS Working Paper 128

source_refs.claim: Separately admissible categorical causal marginals need not glue into a counterfactually consistent joint SCM; compatibility can be represented through response functions.
source_refs.author: Luigi Gresele, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas M. Kübler, Elke Kirschbaum, Bernhard Schölkopf, and Dominik Janzing

open_problems.why_unsolved: Local recoupling preserves each branch marginal, but counterfactual histories shared across levels impose consistency identities, and dormant descendants remain part of the complete FFRCISTG system. The one-step-ahead single-world independences must hold for every fixed parent assignment, not merely along realized histories. Shahn's backward proof leaves this global construction implicit, while Gresele et al. show in an adjacent SCM setting that locally valid causal marginals can fail to glue. The decisive obstacle is therefore a global extension argument, not another local coupling calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A projection-and-lift theorem equating the recursively feasible arrays with the projection of the complete finite FFRCISTG response-type simplex, including an explicit dormant-branch sampler and either projection equality in the two-stage binary-action, three-outcome kill test or a concrete nonliftable counterexample.

writing_exemplar.why: Its backward-recursion sharpness argument states the exact local-to-global claim whose causal-model semantics require completion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observed SMART histories identify branch marginals -> local couplings control branchwise oracle maxima -> backward recursion suggests sharp global bounds -> sharpness requires one complete FFRCISTG lift across realized and dormant branches

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each fixed intervention by its SWIG and certify the extended-g-formula factorization and single-world independence relations for the constructed counterfactual array.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lift must satisfy precisely the single-world semantics that SWIGs encode, rather than only reproduce terminal marginal distributions.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode categorical mechanisms by response functions, impose marginal-projection constraints linearly, and construct or separate a compatible global model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The treatment-tree lift is a causal marginal problem whose extra structure is FFRCISTG consistency and single-world independence.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize every attainable pmf of the maximum of finitely many discrete potential outcomes with fixed, possibly unequal action marginals, rather than only the pointwise-extremal CDFs.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives thresholdwise sharp CDF envelopes and uses a continuous maximal coupling, but does not characterize all attainable discrete maximum pmfs.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs maximally dependent variables attaining an extremal maximum law but does not describe every attainable maximum law for unequal discrete marginals.
source_refs.author: Tze Leung Lai and Herbert Robbins
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Distributions of random-set selections are characterized through capacity inequalities, providing a general existence framework but not the proposed chain reduction.
source_refs.author: Zvi Artstein

open_problems.why_unsolved: With atoms, a candidate pmf must allocate exact-threshold mass while satisfying nested CDF restrictions, and separately chosen thresholdwise couplings need not arise from one joint coupling. Lai–Robbins supplies an extremal construction, while Artstein's general selection theorem ordinarily requires a larger family of subset inequalities. The missing step is to prove that the ordered support and maximum map reduce those compatibility restrictions exactly to the action-CDF and point-mass inequalities, or to exhibit an omitted obstruction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff theorem proving that q is the law of max_a X_a exactly when F_q(k)<=F_a(k) for every action and threshold and q(k)<=sum_a p_a(k) for every atom, together with an attaining coupling and a separating dual certificate when the conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its oracle-personalization motivation and transition from binary success to the outcome distribution supply the closest problem formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Implementable DTRs use observed history -> an oracle can exploit latent response type -> oracle performance depends on cross-world maxima -> discrete clinical outcomes require the entire attainable maximum law rather than two CDF envelopes

method_exemplars.technique: Translate coupling existence into random-selection capacity inequalities and exploit the finite total order to seek a reduced determining class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired iff is an existence characterization for a distribution constrained to be a selection induced by action-specific outcomes.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the interval rearrangement of uniform mass used to construct maximally dependent variables, replacing one extremal envelope by prescribed atom allocations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest constructive simultaneous-threshold coupling argument for a maximum.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate coupling functionals through the optimal-transport dual and derive root-n limits and bootstrap inference for dual sample analogues.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Linear support functionals of the attainable-q polytope are finite optimal-transport values.

open_problems.open_problem: Compress the sharp full-law identified set for a discrete oracle DTR outcome into a formulation polynomial in outcome support times treatment-tree size, with exact membership and support-function dual certificates.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives scalar backward recursions for CDF endpoints but no representation of the complete set of attainable pmf vectors or its support function.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: The paper derives sharp random-set and optimal-transport bounds for joint-potential-outcome functionals, with generic LP implementations whose scale remains material.
source_refs.author: Thomas M. Russell

source_refs.claim: The categorical response-function construction provides a full global-polytope benchmark but grows with the complete response-type representation.
source_refs.author: Luigi Gresele, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas M. Kübler, Elke Kirschbaum, Bernhard Schölkopf, and Dominik Janzing

open_problems.why_unsolved: The complete response-type LP is exponential in the number of counterfactual nodes, whereas Shahn's recursion returns only one threshold endpoint at a time. Russell's general random-set LP does not exploit the laminar treatment-tree structure or address the conditional-probability denominators created by intervention histories. The missing proof must show both that reach-probability rescaling makes every coefficient linear in observed multinomial cells and that the resulting local-flow formulation has exactly the same projection as the full counterfactual model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An O(K times tree-size) linear extended formulation whose projection equals the full FFRCISTG oracle-pmf set, with strong-duality theorems yielding exact membership and support certificates and a polynomial-time sampler attaining every feasible point.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from unidentified response-type dependence to sharp random-set optimization best frames why an exact computational characterization matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization identifies potential-outcome marginals but not dependence -> oracle functionals are partially identified -> generic response-type programs are sharp but large -> the treatment tree may admit a compact exact formulation for the entire oracle law

method_exemplars.technique: Express counterfactual compatibility through a core determining class of random-set capacity inequalities and analyze the associated primal and dual LPs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested membership and support certificates are a whole-distribution, tree-structured specialization of this architecture.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit linear projection maps from a full response-function simplex to observable and causal marginal parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the full-model benchmark against which the tree-sized extended formulation must establish projection equality.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate optimal-transport support values through dual sample analogues and derive their root-n limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every linear functional of the proposed oracle-law polytope is an optimization-defined coupling functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop intervention-reach-adaptive whole-set confidence inference and matching local minimax risk bounds for the polyhedral identified set of the discrete oracle-outcome distribution in a finite SMART.

source_refs.claim: The paper states that repeated maxima, minima, and truncation make endpoint inference nonstandard, that the ordinary bootstrap may fail, and that time-varying inference remains future work.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: The paper documents plug-in failure and develops inference for sharp ordinal treatment-benefit bounds in a static two-arm problem.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs uniformly valid calibrated-projection intervals for smooth functionals of parameters constrained by moment inequalities.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.excerpt: The extra survival factor in this observed-law divergence is the load-bearing step.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The target is a random polytope rather than one regular endpoint: active faces switch when action CDFs cross, union bounds saturate, or atom constraints bind, so pointwise intervals and naive bootstrap procedures do not give uniform whole-set coverage. Known randomization permits finite-sample multinomial inversion, but its diameter should deteriorate with rare intervention reach. The adjacent POMDP proposal supplies a rare-history observed-law Le Cam construction; transferring it requires replacing filtered-reset likelihood calculations by nodewise multinomial perturbations that remain inside the liftable FFRCISTG model and move a selected support face.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous multinomial confidence region mapped through LP feasibility to an outer oracle-pmf set with finite-sample 1-alpha whole-set coverage, together with matching upper and lower local minimax rates for Hausdorff or support-function loss indexed by intervention reach and active-face geometry.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly connects oracle-personalization bounds to the nonregular inferential obstacle in time-varying treatment settings.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp oracle bounds quantify personalization potential -> SMART probabilities must be estimated -> recursive maxima and truncation create changing active faces -> clinical use requires honest simultaneous coverage of the complete oracle-law set

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze atom-driven active constraints responsible for plug-in failure and construct valid inference for sharp ordinal benefit bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its static discrete causal bounds have the closest nonregular face-switching behavior to the local maximum-law constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert studentized moment inequalities using bootstrap-calibrated constraint relaxation and repeated feasibility optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Membership and support queries for the oracle-law polytope reduce to finitely many estimated linear inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its observed-filtration Le Cam alternatives and explicit rare-path KL accounting, replacing latent survival by SMART intervention reach and scalar separation by polytope-face displacement.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both lower bounds require a causal target to move along a rare history while the induced observed laws remain close.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the oracle-outcome distribution set in a two-stage discrete SMART under NPSEM-IE and determine exactly when its cross-world restrictions make the set strictly smaller than the FFRCISTG set.

source_refs.claim: The intervention hierarchy associates different identifying functionals with FFRCISTG and NPSEM-IE and shows that model choice can change identifying content.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: The FFRCISTG sharpness proof uses freedom to associate counterfactual subtrees corresponding to incompatible actions.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: Categorical response-function compatibility can shrink regions obtained from separately specified causal marginals.
source_refs.author: Luigi Gresele, Julius von Kügelgen, Jonas M. Kübler, Elke Kirschbaum, Bernhard Schölkopf, and Dominik Janzing

open_problems.why_unsolved: Shahn's local association step relies on single-world freedom. NPSEM-IE instead places all responses generated by one structural mechanism in common error blocks and imposes cross-world independence restrictions, so arbitrary branchwise recoupling need not be realizable. The model hierarchy is known, and response-function compatibility tools exist, but neither literature characterizes a dynamic cross-regime maximum or determines which observed SMART laws expose a strict difference.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite response-function characterization of the two-stage NPSEM-IE oracle-pmf set, a proof that it is contained in the FFRCISTG set, and necessary-and-sufficient observed-law conditions for equality versus an explicit strictness witness.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing centers the fact that the identifying content of a causal query can depend on counterfactual-model semantics.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Complex counterfactual queries depend on intervention semantics -> FFRCISTG and NPSEM-IE impose different cross-world restrictions -> an oracle maximum combines incompatible regimes -> its identified set can reveal when the distinction has observable consequences

method_exemplars.technique: Translate the target into model-specific intervention responses and compare the counterfactual factorizations licensed by FFRCISTG and NPSEM-IE.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution first requires isolating exactly which cross-world restrictions the oracle maximum invokes.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate categorical response functions and impose global counterfactual compatibility through linear projection constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This provides the natural finite benchmark for testing whether locally coupled treatment branches admit a shared structural-error representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate optimization-defined coupling extrema through primal-dual sample analogues and directionally regular limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Support values of the stronger-model oracle set remain coupling-dependent optimization targets after additional structural constraints are imposed.

open_problems.open_problem: Identify or sharply tighten the distribution of an oracle dynamic-treatment outcome by fusing multiple SMARTs under history-specific transportability of response-state transitions.

source_refs.claim: Multiple point-treatment experiments identify joint potential-outcome distributions under transportable state-transition probabilities and a full-column-rank condition.
source_refs.author: Peng Wu and Xiaojie Mao

source_refs.claim: The oracle time-varying strategy bounds use one sequentially randomized law and do not fuse distinct SMARTs.
source_refs.author: Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: Dynamic-regime welfare can be partially ordered using linear programs, but the cross-regime oracle maximum distribution is not identified.
source_refs.author: Sukjin Han
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Wu and Mao's dataset-indicator rank argument concerns a flat point-treatment response-type vector. A SMART instead produces history-indexed transitions, and different trials may randomize different treatment menus or embed different regimes. The first proof step that changes is the mixture equation: it becomes a block-triangular system indexed by reachable histories, while transportability should be required only for scientifically corresponding transitions. The located literature contains the single-SMART oracle bounds and the point-treatment multi-experiment theorem, but no longitudinal bridge between them.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient block-rank or completeness condition under explicit history-specific transportability assumptions that point-identifies the oracle pmf, or otherwise an exact fused polytope proved strictly tighter than each single-SMART set, with a constrained estimator and limit law.

writing_exemplar.why: It explicitly motivates recovery of cross-world dependence through heterogeneous experimental datasets.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: One experiment reveals potential-outcome marginals but not their joint law -> heterogeneous experiments change response-type mixtures -> transportable transitions plus rank recover cross-world dependence -> multiple SMARTs may recover the oracle dynamic-outcome distribution

method_exemplars.technique: Use dataset membership as an instrument, form response-type mixture equations, and prove uniqueness through a full-column-rank condition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The dynamic problem replaces the paper's flat mixture matrix with a history-indexed block system while preserving its algebraic recovery logic.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the recovered response-type distribution by constrained least squares and transfer the consistency and asymptotic-normality proof to the block system.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once block-rank identification holds, the dynamic target is again a smooth function of a finite linear inverse.

method_exemplars.technique: Use backward recursion to map history-specific counterfactual distributions into the oracle maximum target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After multi-trial fusion identifies or restricts local response states, this recursion supplies the destination functional.

literature_map:
Shahn (2026, arXiv:2608.03133) is the exact anchor: it recursively bounds oracle time-varying treatment performance under FFRCISTG and claims simultaneous sharp CDF envelopes for bounded continuous outcomes.
Its proof selects branch distributions separately and invokes unrestricted association across incompatible actions; a complete dormant-branch FFRCISTG lift is not written out.
Lai and Robbins (1976, PNAS, doi:10.1073/pnas.73.2.286) is the static extremal-maximum coupling anchor, not a characterization of every discrete maximum law.
Artstein (1983, Israel Journal of Mathematics, doi:10.1007/BF02762891) characterizes random-set selection distributions by capacity inequalities and is the closest route to the local discrete iff.
Richardson and Robins (2013, CSSS Working Paper 128) provides the authoritative SWIG and FFRCISTG single-world semantics and explicitly accommodates dynamic regimes.
Shpitser and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2016, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1411.2127) distinguishes FFRCISTG from NPSEM-IE and shows why model strength can change identifying content.
Gresele et al. (2022, ICML, arXiv:2202.01300) shows that locally admissible categorical causal marginals can fail to glue and represents global compatibility with response functions.
Russell (2021, JBES, doi:10.1080/07350015.2019.1684300) provides sharp random-set and optimal-transport LP machinery for joint-potential-outcome functionals but not a tree-sized oracle-law formulation.
Ober-Reynolds (2023, arXiv:2311.09435) supplies dual optimal-transport estimators, root-n limits, and bootstrap inference for coupling-dependent causal functionals.
Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory) is the classical treatment-effect-distribution bounds and nonstandard-inference anchor.
Huang et al. (2017, Biostatistics, doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxw049) demonstrates atom-induced plug-in failure for sharp ordinal treatment-benefit bounds.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica, arXiv:1601.00934) and Beresteanu–Molinari (2008, Econometrica) provide projection and set-valued inference templates, but not finite-SMART whole-polytope inversion.
Galanter et al. (2024, American Journal of Epidemiology) reinforces the clinical oracle-personalization motivation in a static setting without longitudinal full-law results.
Wu and Mao (2026 revision, arXiv:2504.20470) identifies point-treatment joint potential outcomes from multiple experiments using transportable transitions and rank, leaving the multiple-SMART analogue open.
Han (2023, JASA, doi:10.1080/01621459.2023.2238941) partially orders dynamic-regime welfare by LP; neither it nor standard Q/A-learning targets the distribution of the latent oracle maximum.
